open_points.subject: create a project after the created project changes
open_points.text: “a retried create never makes a second project while the first keeps its values” does not define whether “keeps its values” means that the project still retains its create-replay facts, or that every value originally supplied remains unchanged
open_points.question: After an ordinary accepted change to the first project, such as correcting its display name, alias, customer, or object, does retrying its original create still identify that project and avoid creating another, or has the duplicate-prevention guarantee ended; and if it has ended, is the retry a new create or a refusal?
options: The retry still returns the existing project with its current values and never creates a second project until anonymisation or deletion removes the replay facts.
Any change from the originally created values ends replay recognition, so the retry is treated as a new create and may mint a second project.
The original request is still recognized, but because the current values differ, the retry is refused and creates nothing.
open_points.default_guess: The retry returns the existing project with its current values and cannot create a second project unless anonymisation or deletion removed the facts used to recognize it.

witness.initial: Owner created active project P with request id Q, display name A, object O and revision 1; P retains Q as State 1 requires.
events: Owner corrects P's display name from A to B, producing revision 2 while the create request id Q remains.
Owner retries the original create request Q with the original creation values after losing or delaying its first answer.
outcomes: Registry recognizes Q and returns P with its current name B; no second project exists.
Because P no longer “keeps its values,” Registry either mints a new active project with name A or refuses the request as differing from P.
witness.observer: The owner and every catalogue-reading trusted service see either one project, two projects, or a refusal.
